246265.title: Open Storage Reinstallation
246265.overview: MMCA Cheongju is Korea's first 'visible storage' art museum, built inside a former tobacco factory so that visitors can see works normally kept in the vaults. This is the permanent open-storage display.

396296.title: Immersive Hall: Iseongsanseong, Command of the Han River
396296.overview: A media installation on the mountain fortress of Iseongsanseong, built to control the Han River corridor in the era of the Three Kingdoms.

249345.title: Greece to Rome, Rome to Greece
249345.venue: Grand Auditorium, National Museum of Korea

301234.title: A Walk Through the Archives: Parks of Seoul
301234.venue: Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

295982.title: Dinosaur AR Trick Art
295982.venue: Ainuri Theater, Hwaseong Children's Cultural Center

269031.title: Donated Works Gallery Reopening
269031.overview: The National Museum's gallery of donated collections, reopened after redisplay. The museum itself is free to enter and among the largest in Asia — worth half a day on any Seoul itinerary.

341122.title: Museum Week: Full Skeleton of a Baird's Beaked Whale

321034.title: Seonyu Damdam: Landscapes in the Time of Seonyudo

331942.title: MMCA Gwacheon Permanent Exhibition: Modern and Contemporary Korean Art II
331942.overview: The standing survey of Korean modern and contemporary art at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art's Gwacheon branch — the best single overview of the field, in a hillside building beside Seoul Grand Park.

336194.title: Special Storage: MMCA Drawings and Japanese Contemporary Prints

339644.title: SeMA Public Space Project: A Dance That Crosses Forever
339644.venue: Seoul Museum of Art, Seosomun Main Branch
339644.overview: Seoul Museum of Art occupies the former Supreme Court building next to Deoksugung Palace, and admission to the main branch is free.

366684.title: Go Hui-dong House Museum: Evergreen — The Character of the Scholar
366684.overview: The preserved home and studio of Go Hui-dong, regarded as Korea's first Western-style painter, tucked into the lanes near Changdeokgung Palace.

366683.title: Park No-soo Art Museum: Landscape and the Study of Things
366683.overview: The hanok-and-Western hybrid house where the ink painter Park No-soo lived and worked, in the Seochon quarter west of Gyeongbokgung. The garden alone justifies the visit.

347140.title: Bright and Colourful: Dongja Statues
347140.overview: A thematic display of dongja — the child attendant figures that appear in Korean Buddhist temples and funerary art, painted in vivid colours.

368065.title: Kang Ju-hyun: Irregular Forms of Connection
368065.overview: An outdoor sculpture project at the contemporary art museum in Jeju's Jeoji Artist Village, on the island's quieter western side.

345441.title: MMCA Masterpieces from Abroad: Water Lilies and Chandelier
345441.overview: A collection show built around the national museum's holdings of international art, opening the vaults to the public as contemporary museums increasingly do.

371407.title: Islamic Art: A Journey of Radiant Light

359174.title: Buddhist Art of Gangwon: The Path to Enlightenment
359174.overview: Gangwon's mountains hold some of Korea's oldest temples, and this branch display gathers the Buddhist art that came out of them.

360633.title: NEW! The Gyeongju: A Chronicle
360633.venue: Alcheon Art Museum, Gyeongju Arts Center
360633.overview: An immersive media retelling of Gyeongju's history as capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years — useful context before walking the burial mounds and temples outside.

362073.title: Invisible Actors
362073.overview: Photographs by Jo Kyung-jae, who trained as a Meisterschüler at the Münster Academy of Fine Arts and works on what falls outside the camera's limited frame.

365902.title: Collection Display: Lee Ungno, An Artist of His Time
365902.overview: Lee Ungno spent his later career in Paris turning Korean calligraphic line into abstraction. The museum devoted to him in Daejeon holds the standing collection display.

368064.title: 10/10: Ten Years of Choices
368064.venue: Jeju Museum of Art Kim Tschang-yeul
368064.overview: Kim Tschang-yeul spent five decades painting water drops, and donated the works that founded this museum on Jeju.

368076.title: Collection Show: Blanc Black Panorama
368076.price: Adults 4,000 won · youth and soldiers 2,000 · children 1,000

369570.title: The Origin: Plaster Casts, the First Form
369570.overview: The sculptor Moon Shin built this museum himself on a hillside above Masan harbour, and it holds the plaster originals behind his bronze work.

371541.title: University Archive Exhibition: 1996, One Step of the Dance School
371541.venue: Korea National University of Arts, Seokgwan Campus

384575.title: The Freest Path
384575.price: Adults 2,000 won · youth 1,000 · children 500 · seniors and infants free
384575.overview: Rhee Seundja left Korea for Paris in 1951 and built a body of abstract painting drawn from Korean landscape memory. The museum stands in her home city of Jinju.

369772.title: ACC Film and Video: Apparatuses of Asia
369772.venue: ACC Creation Space 2, Asia Culture Center
369772.overview: Moving image treated as an apparatus in its own right, reassembling community history and perception through recording, re-enactment and rewriting. Held at the Asia Culture Center, built on the site of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising.

364986.title: MMCA Performing Arts 2026: The Time of the Detective
364986.overview: A cross-disciplinary programme using the figure of the detective — and the detective's sustained attention — to examine how time is experienced in contemporary life.

373408.title: Interlude for the Body: Somok Jang Semi

374183.title: Cheongju Gallery One: Exhibition Space Applications

374617.title: House: Linking Two Sculptors
374617.overview: Set in the house where the sculptor Choi Man-lin lived and worked, now a district museum in the hills of Seongbuk.

375306.title: GOOD MORNING MR. PAIK & JUNG — Jung Ki-yong Collection: A Map of Friendship
375306.overview: Works and correspondence tracing the friendship between Nam June Paik — the Korean-born founder of video art — John Cage and Joseph Beuys.

376586.title: Gana Art Collection: Beneath Technology — Scenes at the Threshold
376586.venue: Seoul Museum of Art, Seosomun Main Branch

372673.title: Sculpture Dreams: Olympic Sculpture Project #02
372673.overview: SOMA sits inside Olympic Park among the outdoor sculptures commissioned for the 1988 Games — the largest collection of its kind in Korea, and free to walk through.

376498.title: Clayarch Gimhae 20th Anniversary: Folds and Layers
376498.overview: A museum devoted to ceramic art and architecture, its own facade clad in fired tiles. Gimhae has been a pottery centre since the Gaya confederacy.

377100.title: Lee Jung-yoon: The Singing House
377100.overview: Held in a house designed by Kim Chung-up, the first Korean architect to train under Le Corbusier.

364987.title: MMCA Film and Video 2026
364987.overview: The museum cinema's year-round programme of experimental film, documentary and art cinema across eras and forms.

364985.title: Bang Hai Ja: Scattering the Light of the Mind
364985.overview: Bang Hai Ja (1937–2022) worked between Korea and France, building a body of luminous abstract painting from both traditions. Timed to the 140th anniversary of Korea–France relations.

378375.title: Andong Byeolgung: Layers of Time
378375.overview: Seoul's craft museum occupies a former school beside Anguk Station, on the site of the Joseon-era Andong Byeolgung palace annex. Free admission.

385359.title: A Quiet Problem: Kim Tschang-yeul's Newspaper Works
385359.venue: Jeju Museum of Art Kim Tschang-yeul
385359.overview: The series in which Kim Tschang-yeul painted his signature water drops onto newsprint, letting the text show through.

386847.title: Inagoe: A Strange Monster That Looks Like Me

388570.title: Even a Cat May Look at a King

383876.title: K-Museum Touring Exhibition: Connection and Expansion
383876.venue: Chung Young Yang Embroidery Museum, Sookmyung Women's University
383876.overview: A specialist museum of Korean and world embroidery, holding one of the most significant collections of its kind.

378574.title: The Title Exhibition
378574.overview: An exhibition about film titles — the shortest and most forceful language by which we first meet a work. Held at the Korean Film Archive's museum, which is free and pairs well with its screening programme.

292206.title: Road Movie: Korean and Japanese Art Since 1945
292206.overview: Korea and Japan have moved through a long, close and difficult history. This exhibition asks what relationship their contemporary art has held since 1945 — an unusually direct treatment of the subject by a national museum.

380356.title: What We Were at University
380356.venue: Seoul Museum of History of Everyday Life

380357.title: Yoo Youngkuk: The Mountain Is Within Me
380357.venue: Seoul Museum of Art, Seosomun Main Branch
380357.overview: Yoo Youngkuk reduced the Korean mountain to blocks of saturated colour and became one of the founding figures of Korean abstraction. A major retrospective, free to enter.

385021.title: National Treasures on Tour: Treasures in Your Neighbourhood
385021.overview: Part of a programme bringing designated National Treasures out of the major institutions and into regional museums — here, a museum devoted to Korean bronze bells.

387676.title: Blue Heart: Mangroves
387676.overview: The national maritime museum sits on reclaimed land off Yeongdo island in Busan and is free to enter, with an aquarium inside.

382397.title: Grown on Drink, Living in Writing
382397.overview: An exhibition at the literary museum for the poet Byeon Yeong-ro, whose pen name Suju gives the museum its name.

394839.title: Kim Tschang-yeul: Traces of a Water Drop
394839.overview: The opening exhibition of the newly restored house of Kim Tschang-yeul, the painter who devoted his career to the water drop.

384083.title: Again, Us on That Road: Muttering on the Street
384083.overview: Gi Hyeong-do died at 29 in 1989, leaving a single posthumous collection that became one of the most influential books in modern Korean poetry.

384561.title: Kwon Byung-jun: You, In My Heart

394039.title: DMZ: A Corridor of Wind
394039.venue: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
394039.overview: The Demilitarized Zone has been closed to people for seventy years and has become, by accident, one of the best-preserved habitats in the peninsula. The museum sits on Gwanghwamun Square and is free.

394117.title: K-Art 2026: Translating Tradition, Imagining the Future

375294.title: Sarira Reliquary from the Hwangnyongsa Wooden Pagoda
375294.overview: Marking fifty years since excavation began at Hwangnyongsa, once the greatest temple of Silla. Its nine-storey wooden pagoda is gone, but the foundation stone that held the reliquary survives, and the sarira containers found in and beneath it are shown here.

384576.title: Nomura Motoyuki, a Star Over Cheonggyecheon
384576.overview: A Japanese pastor who photographed and supported the shanty communities along Cheonggyecheon during Korea's industrialisation, and later donated his archive to the city.

384573.title: Eternity in an Instant: Photographs of Jeju by Kim Young-gap
384573.overview: Kim Young-gap photographed Jeju's wind and grasslands for twenty years until Lou Gehrig's disease took his ability to press the shutter. The donated works are shown at the national museum on the island. Free.

386987.title: Too Good to Keep to Myself: 30th Anniversary Donation Exhibition

364984.title: This Is (Not) Conceptual Art
364984.overview: A survey of the conceptual strand in Korean contemporary art — work that put idea, language, process and context ahead of material form. MMCA Seoul sits beside Gyeongbokgung Palace in the Samcheong-dong gallery quarter.
